preview.subject: HANGS Construction Services 2026 estimated tax, December payment
preview.body:
Hi,

The December 15 estimate is coming up and I want to get it right this time. So far this year we have paid what we paid each quarter last year: $12,075.00 in April and June, and $16,000.00 in September when I saw the year was running ahead. Our 2025 return went in on October 13 with total tax of $59,302.33.

Attached are the full-year projection and the EFTPS history. The interim taxable income for the first three, six and nine months is in the folder; the winter months were slow and the January 9 bonus to Celeste came out of Q1.

Two questions:
- How much should we pay on December 15, and are we short for the earlier quarters?
- The EFTPS confirmation for the June 15 payment shows tax period 12/2025. I think I picked the wrong year. Does that matter?

Thanks,
Morgan Lee
Controller, HANGS Construction Services LLC

sources.title: Guidance on determining a corporation's estimated tax payment (Form 1120-W is historical)

passages.q: Is Form 1120-W still the worksheet to use?
passages.a: Form 1120-W, Estimated Tax for Corporations, and the Instructions for Form 1120-W are now historical. The 2022 Form 1120-W (released in 2021) and the 2022 Instructions for Form 1120-W (released in 2021) were the last revision of both the form and its instructions. Publication 542, Corporations, the Instructions for Form 1120 ... will be updated to include guidance on determining a corporation's estimated tax payments.

passages.q: How and by when must the remaining payments be made?
passages.a: Corporations must use electronic funds transfer (EFT) to make all federal tax deposits (such as deposits of employment, excise, and corporate income tax). ... EFTPS accepts same day payments of $1 million or less if the payment is submitted before 3:00 p.m. Eastern time on a business day.

passages.q: Which annualization periods and amounts apply, and how is each installment chosen?
passages.a: Use Option 1 or Option 2 only if the corporation elected to do so by filing Form 8842 ... standard option 3 3 6 9 ... standard option 4 4 2 1.33333 ... Line 35. Enter in each column of line 35 25% of the amount from page 1, Part I, line 5. ... Line 38. For each installment, enter the smaller of line 34 or line 37 on line 38.

passages.q: How long does a short installment draw the penalty, and which installment does a payment go to?
passages.a: The penalty is figured for the period of underpayment using the underpayment rate determined under section 6621. The period of underpayment generally runs from the installment due date to the earlier of the date the underpayment is actually paid or the 15th day of the 4th month after the close of the tax year. ... A payment of estimated tax is applied against unpaid required installments in the order in which installments are required to be paid, regardless of the installment to which the payment pertains.

passages.q: Which 2025 return sets the safe harbor if the 2025 return is later amended?
passages.a: In these instructions, "return" generally refers to the corporation's original return. However, an amended return is considered the original return if the amended return is filed by the due date (including extensions) of the original return. Also, for purposes of determining a required installment ..., if an amended return is filed for the prior tax year, then the return for the "prior tax year" includes the amended return, but only if the amended return is filed before the applicable installment due date.

sources.title: Interest rates remain the same for the fourth quarter of 2026 (IR-2026-98)

passages.q: Did the rate change for October to December 2026?
passages.a: The Internal Revenue Service today announced that interest rates will remain the same for the calendar quarter beginning Oct. 1, 2026. ... 7% for underpayments (taxes owed but not fully paid).

passages.q: When are a calendar-year corporation's installments due, and when may last year's tax be used?
passages.a: Installment payments are due by the 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months of the corporation's tax year. Example 1. Your corporation's tax year ends December 31. Installment payments are due on April 15, June 15, September 15, and December 15. ... Method 2. Each required installment is 25% of the income tax shown on the corporation's return for the previous year. ... the return must have been for a full 12 months, and the return must have shown a positive tax liability (not zero).

passages.q: What does the estimated tax worksheet compute?
passages.a: This worksheet may be used as a guide in figuring the required estimated tax installments. ... Enter the tax shown on the corporation's prior year's tax return. ... Enter the smaller of line 8 or line 9. ... Required installments. Enter 25% of line 10. ... Form 1120-W, Estimated Tax for Corporations, is now historical.

passages.q: What must go with the 2026 return if the annualized method is used, and should HANGS catch up now?
passages.a: An immediate catch-up payment should be made to reduce any penalty resulting from the underpayment of any earlier installments. ... Even if the corporation does not owe a penalty, complete and attach the form to the corporation's tax return if any of the following apply. The annualized income installment method was used to figure any required installment.
2026 interest rates by category ... 4th quarter (Oct-Dec) 3rd quarter (Jul-Sep) 2nd quarter (Apr-Jun) 1st quarter (Jan-Mar) ... Underpayment (corporate and non-corporate) 7% 7% 6% 7%

passages.q: Can the estimated tax penalty be removed for reasonable cause?
passages.a: Reasonable cause is determined on a case-by-case basis considering all the facts and circumstances of your situation. ... Reasonable cause doesn't apply to certain penalties such as the estimated tax penalty.

sources.title: 26 U.S. Code 6655, Failure by corporation to pay estimated income tax
sources.issuer: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School (U.S. Code text)

passages.q: What must HANGS pay in 2026 to avoid the estimated tax penalty?
passages.a: Except as otherwise provided in this section, the amount of any required installment shall be 25 percent of the required annual payment. ... the lesser of (i) 100 percent of the tax shown on the return for the taxable year ..., or (ii) 100 percent of the tax shown on the return of the corporation for the preceding taxable year. Clause (ii) shall not apply if the preceding taxable year was not a taxable year of 12 months, or the corporation did not file a return for such preceding taxable year showing a liability for tax.

passages.q: Is HANGS a large corporation, which could not use last year's tax?
passages.a: The term "large corporation" means any corporation if such corporation (or any predecessor corporation) had taxable income of $1,000,000 or more for any taxable year during the testing period. ... The term "testing period" means the 3 taxable years immediately preceding the taxable year involved. ... the $1,000,000 amount ... shall be divided among such members [of a controlled group].

passages.q: Can the slow first quarter lower the early installments?
passages.a: If the corporation establishes that the annualized income installment or the adjusted seasonal installment is less than the amount determined under subsection (d)(1) ... the amount of such required installment shall be the annualized income installment ... and any reduction in a required installment resulting from the application of this paragraph shall be recaptured by increasing the amount of the next required installment ... for the first 3 months of the taxable year, in the case of the 1st required installment

Left there, it is a 2025 overpayment, not a 2026 installment: the 2nd installment would have been $1,121.40 short from June 15, the 3rd $15,980.90 short now, and the penalty so far $181.73. A person (with Form 2848 on file, or the controller) asks the IRS to move it to 12/2026. If it is not moved before December 15, pay another $12,075.00 then and claim the 2025 overpayment back.

checks.title: ANNUAL-01
checks.detail: The annualized method rests on the controller's closed-month taxable income for 3, 6 and 9 months ($31,420.00, $139,860.00, $248,610.00), not reviewed. The first quarter includes the $30,000.00 officer bonus paid January 9, which annualizing multiplies by 4; a person confirms the interim figures and that no item is an extraordinary item the Form 2220 instructions add after annualizing. Form 2220 with Schedule A must be attached to the 2026 return.

checks.title: PRIOR-01
checks.detail: The safe harbor is the $59,302.33 of tax on the 2025 return filed October 13, 2026, the Form 1120 demo's figure. The 2025 draft left officer pay approval and the related-party advance open; an amended 2025 return filed before December 15 would reset the 4th installment's base. A person confirms no amendment is planned before then.

checks.title: PLAN-01
checks.detail: Unsigned plan. Nothing has been paid or scheduled: $3,905.90 on November 13 and $15,246.43 on December 15, both EFTPS, Form 1120, tax period 12/2026, estimated tax. Paying only the safe harbor leaves about $13,542.47 due April 15, 2027 on the projected tax of $72,844.80; the controller may prefer to pay more in December for cash planning. The projection changes with the December results.

checks.title: The large-corporation test: taxable income for the three years before 2026
checks.detail: 2025 Form 1120 filed October 13, 2026 on extension: 12 months, taxable income $282,392.05, total tax $59,302.33. Taxable income for the testing period: 2023 $211,900.00, 2024 $230,000.00, 2025 $282,392.05. None is $1,000,000 or more, there are no loss carryovers, and the company is in no controlled group, so HANGS is not a large corporation: last year's tax can set all four 2026 installments.

checks.detail: Pay $3,905.90 now (settling Friday, November 13) to stop the penalty on the 3rd installment, and $15,246.43 on Tuesday, December 15 for the 4th. With the $40,150.00 already paid that is $59,302.33, the full prior-year safe harbor. The 2026 tax is projected at $72,844.80, so about $13,542.47 remains due with the return on April 15, 2027, without penalty. Both payments: EFTPS, Form 1120, tax period 12/2026, estimated tax.
